title: EPA's Chemical-Detecting Plane Fails to Meet Demand
excerpt: The EPA's chemical-detecting Cessna aircraft is flying fewer missions and failing to deliver real-time data during toxic emergencies.
body_html:
The United States Environmental Protection Agency utilizes a specialized Cessna aircraft designed to detect chemicals during disasters and toxic emergencies. However, reports indicate that this key monitoring tool is no longer functioning effectively.

According to available details, the plane is currently flying fewer missions than required. Furthermore, it is no longer capable of providing real-time data to disaster responders, even as the frequency of toxic emergencies continues to rise.
